Three starts captures quality gain restarting — benchmarks across wide range datasets improvement curve bends early (knee n ≈ 3–4); higher-quality results, prefer DropAdd(), whose tabu search escapes plateau restarts . number random starts can configured via nSeeds argument. strategies select peripheral seeds available via strategy argument; described PickPoint(). best solution requested strategies used. large datasets points associated natural coordinates, may feasible compute store N×N distances. cases, distance function may take place distance matrix. function passed one index time, must return distance point. title: MaxMin 0.0.0.9000 (development)
text: Initial release: tiered toolbox Max-Min Diversity Problem (MMDP / discrete p-dispersion). FarFirst(): deterministic farthest-first selection distance matrix, Euclidean coordinates (points =), -demand distance-column oracle (pass column function d, N =) spaces coordinate embedding; oracle may report self-distance (length N) omit (length N - 1), whichever simpler compute. default seed runs best--three ensemble "random_furthest" starts (whose pivots drawn session RNG; set seed reproducible selection, supply via pivots argument) keeps best MinDist(). deterministic O(N) anchors ("anti_centroid", "peripheral") costlier O(N²) anchors ("diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") available opt-strategies. DropAdd(): DropAdd tabu search (Porumbel et al. 2011); accepts dist object, distance matrix, coordinate matrix (points =). ExactMaxMin(): exact node-packing optimum (Sayyady & Fathi 2016) via highs MILP backend. Grasp(): GRASP path relinking (Resende et al. 2010), dense-matrix-refinement metaheuristic attains highest T_k package’s methods small medium instances. MinDist(): k-centre objective (minimum pairwise distance). PickPoint(): exposes peripheral seed indices directly.
